newsitem.title: USA: DTB adds two U.S. firms to its membership.
newsitem.headline: DTB adds two U.S. firms to its membership.

text.p: Deutsche Terminboerse, the German futures and options exchange, said Friday that Chase Manhattan Bank in New York and Rosenthal, Collins in Chicago have joined its list of members based in the United States.
"The trial to get new members from abroad is a success," Joerg Franke, general manager of Deutsche Boerse, said at the Futures Industry Association conference here.
Chase and Rosenthal Collins bring to six the number of U.S.-based firms trading on the DTB via its computer terminals, he told a news briefing.
He said about 10 percent of the DTB's total volume of Bund and Bobl futures was traded from the U.S.
The DTB has 164 members, 72 of whom are non-German members trading on screens in eight countries.

The DTB recently launched a two-year Schatz government bond futures contract, and if the German Finance Ministry and Bundesbank decide to issue 30-year debt, the DTB will consider futures on 15- to 30-year bonds, Franke said.
